texts.orig: Friction is an energy loss due to viscous shear of the flowing fluid.
texts.text: Friction is an energy loss due to viscous shear of the flowing fluid.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In a fluid, molecules are free to move past each other but there may be a little resistance.  This resistance is due to shear forces which must be overcome.
texts.text: In a fluid, molecules are free to move past each other but there may be a little resistance.  This resistance is due to shear forces which must be overcome.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The higher the shear forces, the higher the viscosity.
texts.text: The higher the shear forces, the higher the viscosity.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In a single-phase fluid, most of the liquid is moving along together so there is not much shear in the liquid itself and this friction can usually be ignored.
texts.text: In a single-phase fluid, most of the liquid is moving along together so there is not much shear in the liquid itself and this friction can usually be ignored.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The walls of the pipe, however, will tend to "stick" to the fluid so shear forces between the pipe and the fluid can be quite large and increase as the velocity of the fluid increases.
